messages:
raj: :rotating_light: Root: We are seeing intermittent streaming message duplication and out-of-order fragments for a subset of hosted and dedicated realtime sessions in eu-west. Symptoms started ~10:25 UTC and affect primarily long-lived websocket streams when the mux layer backpressure spikes. Link to live status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2061240000

oncall-bot: Alert triggered by mux-backpressure-monitor (level=high). 42 streams affected across 7 customers. Autotriage assigned to @sam and @elena.

sam: Initial triage: root cause looks like an interaction between the mux connection pooling and our in-flight buffer resizing. Under sustained CPU jitter we were dropping frames which the client TCP stack resends, producing duplicates and re-ordering when reconnects occur.

elena: Mitigation steps deployed at 10:40 UTC: 1) enabled strict per-session sequencing at the mux to de-duplicate frames, 2) throttled new connect ramp to eu-west mux pool, 3) rolled a lightweight kernel parameter change to increase socket recv buffer for mux hosts.

raj: Impact: customers with streaming SLAs may see duplicate or slightly out-of-order events for up to ~2 minutes after reconnect. Not a full outage, but causes user-visible glitches in some streaming apps.

maria: Customer comms draft: "We’re investigating intermittent stream duplication for eu-west customers. We’ve applied mitigations and expect normal ordering to return shortly. We’ll follow up with a post-incident summary." Ready to send once we confirm stable for 30m.

jamal: Confirmed: after mitigations error rate on streaming path dropped from 1.8% -> 0.12% within 6 minutes. Order-preservation checks look good in canary.

elena: Next actions: 1) schedule mux restart window for eu-west to pick up new backpressure patch (non-disruptive canary then rolling), 2) add a sequencing TTL to prevent stray duplicate delivery on reconnect, 3) write mitigations into the playbook.

sam: Temporary workaround for customers wanting immediate fix: toggle client-side strict-seq in SDK (v2.4.1) — we pushed patch and it will cause clients to drop duplicates locally until server-side fix completes. Command for ops:

```
# enable client strict seq flag (ops only)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/feature-flags -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"flag":"client.strict_seq","enabled":true,"scope":"eu-west"}'
```

infrabot: Note: scheduled rolling restart window proposed at 12:30 UTC (eu-west) with 5m canary. Please add any objections within 15m.

raj: Customer list pinned: CUST-301, CUST-488, CUST-999. Engs to prioritize comms if any of those open tickets escalate.

maria: Sent initial comms to impacted accounts at 11:05 UTC. Tracking thread in #customer-success.

oncall-bot: Status update: mitigations applied, active monitoring; severity downgraded to S2 at 11:12 UTC. Will keep channel updated.

elena: Filing incident checklist items now. Postmortem owners: @sam (cause/mitigation) and @elena (fix/deployment). ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow.

raj: Thanks all — please watch alerts and escalate if we see regression. End of thread for status broadcast. :white_check_mark:
